title: German text mixes „typographic“ and "straight" quotes; a blueprint writes degrees as '15 C'
claim: In German, 27 quoted spans across translations/de.json and the card's STRINGS use straight ASCII quotes while 95 use „…“ (25 of the 27 in de.json, e.g. exceptions.config_entry_not_loaded); and blueprints/automation/economy_mode_on_price_peak.yaml's description writes '1.5 C' and '15 C' where every other surface writes °C.
mechanism: Strings were translated at different times by different passes: some kept the English source's ASCII quotes around placeholders and option names, others used German typography; the blueprint description is plain text written without the degree sign.

evidence.machine: box B10 (4 vCPU, Linux, CPython 3.14 venv-ci, Node 22)
evidence.contention_note: a count over file-delivered strings, contention-immune
evidence.unit: count of straight-quoted spans in de strings (translations/de.json + card STRINGS.de) beside 95 typographic ones

instrumented_symbol: custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/translations/de.json (all leaf strings HA renders) and heatpump-optimizer-card.js:STRINGS.de (loaded in a Node vm, the table L() reads); blueprints/automation/economy_mode_on_price_peak.yaml:blueprint.description

perturbation.change: --perturb=de_quotes: de.json's straight-quoted spans rewritten „…“ in memory

metric_definition: regex count of "…" spans (1-80 chars) in de delivered strings, beside the count of „…“ spans
phenomenon_property: Within one language, the user-facing text uses one quotation style and one temperature notation (°C).

null_control.note: the degree count is 0 in de and sv over the same surfaces, so the regex does not read '°C' as bare 'C'

proposed_fix_scope: Normalise de.json (and the 2 card STRINGS.de spans) to „…“; write '1.5 °C' / '15 °C' in the blueprint description. sv/en straight quotes are the majority style there and are not claimed.
